chunks: Wiping the head is upon its forepart.

2- And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me; he said: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Qūlawayh informed me, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Shādhān ibn al-Khalīl al-Naysābūrī, from Maʿmar ibn ʿUmar, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
For wiping the head, the area of three fingers suffices, and likewise the foot.

3- And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from some of his companions, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, concerning a man who performs wudu (ablution) while he is wearing a turban; he said:
He lifts the turban enough to insert his finger, then wipes over the forepart of his head.

4- As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ẓarīf ibn Nāṣiḥ, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who wipes his head from behind while he is wearing a turban, with his finger — does that suffice him? He said: Yes.

So this does not contradict what we have stated earlier, that the wiping should be on the forepart of the head, because it is not impossible for a person to insert his finger from behind and yet wipe with it the forepart of the head. It is also possible that the report was issued by way of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of some of the ʿāmmah.
5- As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about wiping over the head, and he said:

"It is as though I am looking at a fold at the back of my father's neck over which he passes his hand." And I asked him about wudu (ablution): is the head wiped, its front and its back? He said: "It is as though I am looking at a fold on my father's neck which he wipes over."
So the proper way to understand this report is what we mentioned last: interpreting it as taqiyyah and nothing else.

6- And as for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, raising it to Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, concerning wiping the two feet and wiping the head, he said:
The wiping of the head is one stroke from the front of the head and its back, and the wiping of the two feet is their outer side and their inner side.

So the proper way to understand this report as well is taqiyyah, because among the jurists are those who hold the wiping of the two feet and yet also hold that the entire limb is to be covered outwardly and inwardly. It is also possible that what was meant by their outer and inner sides was: forward and backward, as we have explained regarding it.

key_terms.إِصْبَعَهُ: his finger, used here for performing the wiping
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain circumstances
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, the limb to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْعِمَامَةُ: the turban worn on the head
key_terms.الْقَدَمَيْنِ: the two feet, wiped in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, where on the head should the wiping in wudu (ablution) be performed, and how are conflicting hadith understood?
ai.summary: These reports discuss the legal rulings of wiping the head and feet in wudu (ablution), emphasizing that wiping the forepart of the head is sufficient and that even a limited area may suffice. The later reports that seem to permit otherwise are reconciled either by interpretation consistent with wiping the forepart or by being understood as issued in taqiyyah.
